mainTopic: רבי יוחנן's rule that a court arrangement counts like a document in hand, tested through the משנה of a גט without a כתובה and the case of a widow from betrothal (אלמנה מן האירוסין).
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ruling by רבי יוחנן: someone who says 'I already paid' a court-based obligation is not believed, because whatever the court arranges counts as if the other side holds a שטר. רבי חייא בר אבא says this is already taught in the משנה that a woman with only a גט collects her כתובה. רבי יוחנן answers that the idea was hidden there until he lifted the 'shard' and showed the 'pearl.' אביי first rejects the proof: the משנה may deal with a place where no כתובה is written, so the גט itself serves as the כתובה. Then אביי takes this back. If a woman could collect only with a document, how would an אלמנה מן האירוסין ever collect? The heirs could always say 'we paid,' and the חכמים' arrangement would be useless. מר קשישא challenges this: how do we know an אלמנה מן האירוסין gets a כתובה at all? A משנה that says she 'collects everything' may refer only to a case where the husband wrote her a כתובה. On that reading the משנה is still not stating the obvious, because it comes to reject רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The גמרא then starts to show that the word 'everything' supports this reading, and the argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A claim of 'I paid' is not accepted for court-based obligations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's ruling (continued from the previous daf) ends: the person's claim is worthless, because whatever the court arranges is treated like a document held in hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: He has said nothing. What is the reason? Anything that comes from a court arrangement is treated as if the person is holding a document in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יוחנן's ruling and explains why: a claim of payment against a court-based obligation is not believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, without a document, a person who says 'I paid' can be believed. But a debt created by the court is treated as though the creditor is holding a שטר. Someone who holds a שטר is not answered by a bare claim of 'I paid'.

keyTerms.meaning: He said nothing. His claim has no legal value.
Something done or arranged by the court

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, that a court arrangement equals a document, is what the rest of the section tests against the משנה.

phrases.english: He has said nothing.
phrases.notes: This is the end of רבי יוחנן's ruling, which started on the previous daf. The person claiming payment is not believed.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Anything done by the court
is like someone who holds a document in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's ruling begun on the previous daf and gives its reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A claim of 'I paid' against a court-based obligation is rejected, because such an obligation counts as a document in hand.

steps.title: Isn't this already taught in our משנה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא asks רבי יוחנן why he needed to say this, since a משנה already rules that a woman with only a גט collects her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said to רבי יוחנן: Isn't this our משנה? If she produced a גט and has no כתובה with it, she collects her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא challenges רבי יוחנן: your rule seems to be already stated in a משנה, so what are you adding?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה is a court arrangement (תנאי בית דין). The משנה lets the woman collect even without the כתובה document. That looks exactly like רבי יוחנן's idea that a court arrangement works like a document in hand, so his statement seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this our משנה? A way of saying 'this is already taught.'
Marriage contract promising the wife money if the marriage ends

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack saying רבי יוחנן is wrong. It agrees with him and only asks why he needed to say something a משנה already teaches.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to Rabbi Yochanan:
But isn't this our Mishnah?
If she produced a bill of divorce and there is no marriage contract with it,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in כתובות 88b.

phrases.english: she collects her marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבי יוחנן's statement by pointing to an existing משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי יוחנן's statement in step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה already lets a woman collect her כתובה (a court arrangement) without the document, רבי יוחנן's rule adds nothing new.

steps.title: Without me, you wouldn't have found the pearl
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן admits the משנה is the source but says the principle was hidden there until he revealed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If I had not lifted up the broken piece of pottery for you, you would not have found the pearl underneath it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that his statement still matters: it uncovers the reason hidden inside the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives only the ruling, not the reason behind it. רבי יוחנן's contribution is the general principle that explains the ruling. Without him, nobody would have seen that principle in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A pearl. Here, a valuable insight.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If I had not lifted the shard for you,
you would not have found the pearl beneath it.
phrases.notes: The 'pearl' is the principle. The משנה hid it until רבי יוחנן pointed it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי חייא בר אבא's question about why the statement was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Admits the source but claims credit for revealing the reason behind it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's statement is unnecessary because the משנה already says it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is indeed the source, but רבי יוחנן's statement reveals the hidden principle behind its ruling.

steps.title: אביי: The משנה is no proof at all
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues the משנה may deal with a place where no כתובה document is written, so the גט itself serves as the כתובה. That would mean the משנה does not support רבי יוחנן's principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What pearl? Perhaps we are dealing with a place where they do not write a כתובה, so the גט is her כתובה. But in a place where they do write a כתובה: if she holds a כתובה, she collects; if not, she does not collect.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects the idea that the משנה proves רבי יוחנן's rule by offering another way to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a place where no כתובה document is written, the גט is the only proof she was married and divorced, so it works as her כתובה. In a place where a כתובה is written, the משנה would not let her collect without it. So the משנה does not show that a court arrangement alone works like a document.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place where they do not write (a כתובה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says a court arrangement counts as a document in hand. רבי חייא בר אבא saw this in the משנה of a גט without a כתובה. אביי first suggests the משנה may only mean places where the גט itself serves as the כתובה. In the next step he takes this back.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not rejecting רבי יוחנן's rule itself. He only rejects using this משנה as proof for it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
What pearl?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין כּוֹתְבִין כְּתוּבָּה עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Perhaps we are dealing with a place where they do not write a marriage contract,
where the bill of divorce is her marriage contract.
But in a place where they do write a marriage contract,
if she holds a marriage contract, she collects;
if not, she does not collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the משנה-based support that steps 2 and 3 accepted.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not רבי יוחנן's principle itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as limited to places where no כתובה is written, so the גט functions as the document.

steps.title: אביי takes back his objection by asking about a widow from betrothal
steps.stepSummary: אביי retracts his reading. If a woman without a כתובה document could not collect, how would an אלמנה מן האירוסין ever collect?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי then said: What I said is not correct. Suppose we say the משנה is only about a place where no כתובה is written, and that in a place where they do write one, she collects if she holds the כתובה and does not collect if she doesn't. Then with what does a widow from betrothal collect?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now attacks his own earlier objection from step 4. He brings a case that his reading cannot explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 4, in a place where a כתובה is written, a woman can only collect if she physically holds it. But an אלמנה מן האירוסין has no כתובה document and no גט, and she still collects. So there must be some other way she is protected.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said (a sign that the speaker is changing his earlier view)
It is not a correct statement
A widow from betrothal: her husband died after קידושין but before נישואין

phrases.english: Abaye then said:
What I said is not correct,
for if it enters your mind
that we are dealing with a place where they do not write a כתובה,
but in a place where they do write a כתובה,
if she holds a כתובה, she collects;
if not, she does not collect,
then with what does a widow from betrothal collect?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָאו מִלְּתָא הִיא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's own reading in step 4, that the משנה is about a place where no כתובה is written
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a woman collects only with a document in hand, an אלמנה מן האירוסין, who has no document, could never collect.

steps.title: Witnesses to the husband's death are not enough
steps.stepSummary: Suppose she collects by showing witnesses that her husband died. The heirs could still claim they already paid her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say she collects by bringing witnesses that her husband died, then let the heirs claim and say: 'We paid her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible answer to step 5's question and immediately knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses only prove that the husband died. They do not prove she was never paid. Without a document in her hand, the heirs' claim of payment should win.

phrases.english: If you say she collects with witnesses to the husband's death,
let him claim and say: I paid it.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the husband's heir, the one she is asking to pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעֵדֵי מִיתַת בַּעַל – לִטְעוֹן וְלֵימָא: פְּרַעְתִּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to step 5's question and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that witnesses to the death are enough for her to collect
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The witnesses prove the death, not that she was never paid, so the heirs could claim payment.

steps.title: Otherwise the Sages' arrangement would be useless
steps.stepSummary: If the heirs really could claim 'we paid,' the חכמים' arrangement giving her a כתובה would accomplish nothing. So the arrangement itself must protect her like a document in hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: Yes, the heirs really can claim that. Then what did the חכמים accomplish with their arrangement?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the last way out: accepting that the heirs can claim 'I paid.' Doing so would empty the חכמים' arrangement of any value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים gave this widow the right to a כתובה. If the heirs could cancel it every time just by saying 'I paid,' the right would be meaningless. So the arrangement itself must count like a document in her hand, and that is exactly רבי יוחנן's principle.

keyTerms.meaning: What did the Sages accomplish with their arrangement?

steps.whatToRemember: An אלמנה מן האירוסין collects even without any document. This shows that something the court arranges works like a document in hand. אביי's retraction ends up supporting רבי יוחנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This restores the משנה about a woman collecting with only a גט as a real source for רבי יוחנן's principle.

phrases.english: And if you would say: indeed, that is so,

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן מָה הוֹעִילוּ חֲכָמִים בְּתַקָּנָתָן?
phrases.english: if so, what did the Sages accomplish with their arrangement?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכִי נָמֵי, אִם כֵּן מָה הוֹעִילוּ חֲכָמִים בְּתַקָּנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks the option of simply accepting the heirs' claim from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the heirs can defeat her by claiming 'I paid'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That would make the חכמים' arrangement pointless, so the arrangement itself must act as a document in hand.

steps.title: How do we know a widow from betrothal gets a כתובה at all?
steps.stepSummary: מר קשישא בריה דרב חסדא asks רב אשי for the source that an אלמנה מן האירוסין is entitled to a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר קשישא son of רב חסדא said to רב אשי: And a widow from betrothal, who has a כתובה, where do we know that from?
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. It questions the basic assumption that אביי's argument depended on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's whole proof assumed that a widow from betrothal collects a כתובה. If that assumption has no source, the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar Kashisha son of Rav Chisda said to Rav Ashi:
And a widow from betrothal,
that she has a כתובה, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that an אלמנה מן האירוסין collects a כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no source shows she has a כתובה, אביי's argument has no foundation.

steps.title: A suggested source from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a source: a משנה says that a woman widowed or divorced, whether from betrothal or from marriage, collects everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes from what we learned in a משנה: If she was widowed or divorced, whether from betrothal or from marriage, she collects everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible source to answer מר קשישא's question. This sets up the next step, which will test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly mentions a widow from betrothal collecting. At first glance, this seems to prove she has a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that is often about to be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say from what we learned in a משנה:
If she was widowed or divorced,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הָאֵירוּסִין וּבֵין מִן הַנִּישּׂוּאִין –
phrases.english: whether from betrothal or from marriage,
she collects everything,

steps.raayaObject: That an אלמנה מן האירוסין is entitled to a כתובה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כתובות: widowed or divorced, from betrothal or marriage, she collects everything

steps.title: Perhaps the משנה is only where he wrote her a כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The משנה may only be talking about a case where the husband actually wrote her a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the משנה is talking about where he wrote one for her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggested source from step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband actually wrote her a כתובה, she has a document, so of course she collects. The משנה therefore does not prove that the חכמים gave every widow from betrothal a כתובה without a document. That leaves אביי's argument in question.

keyTerms.meaning: Where he wrote it for her

steps.confusionAlert: The rejection does not say a widow from betrothal never collects. It only says this משנה cannot prove she collects without a written כתובה.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is where he wrote it for her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source proposed in step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using the כתובות משנה as a source for a widow from betrothal collecting without a written כתובה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may refer only to a case where the husband actually wrote her a כתובה.

steps.title: Why would the משנה teach something so obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection: if the husband wrote her a כתובה, of course she collects. So what is the משנה teaching?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: what is the point of saying this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own rejection from step 10. If the משנה is only about a woman who has a written כתובה, the ruling seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said the משנה may be talking only about a woman whose husband wrote her a כתובה. But if he wrote it, she obviously collects what it says. A משנה does not usually teach obvious things, so this reading seems weak.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible objection)
What is the point of saying it? (this is obvious)
The marriage document that promises the wife money if the marriage ends

phrases.english: And if you would say: what is the point of saying this?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 10 by saying it makes the משנה state something obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading from step 10 that the משנה is about a woman who has a written כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she has a written document, collecting it is obvious, and a משנה would not teach something obvious.

steps.title: The משנה is teaching against רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed to reject רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who holds that the husband wrote the כתובה only on condition that he would marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the view of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who says that the husband wrote the כתובה for her only on the condition that he would marry her. So the משנה needed to teach this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ruling is not obvious, because רבי אלעזר בן עזריה disagrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says a husband writes his promises in the כתובה only with the plan of actually marrying her. So if he dies before the marriage, what he committed to in writing does not count. The משנה says that even a widow from betrothal collects 'everything,' meaning the extra he added as well, and that rejects his view. So the reading from step 10 still works.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring her in as his wife (the full marriage, נישואין)
It was necessary for him (the משנה needed to teach it)

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the rejection in step 10. The proof from the משנה still fails, so we still do not have a source that an אלמנה מן האירוסין gets a כתובה without a written document.

phrases.english: It comes to exclude the view of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה,
who says that he did not write it for her
except on the condition that he would marry her
so it was necessary for the משנה to teach it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11 by showing the ruling is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling has a purpose: it rejects a תנא who disagrees.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Collecting a written כתובה seems too obvious for the משנה to teach.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is needed to reject רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who says the written כתובה depends on the marriage actually happening.

steps.title: The words 'she collects everything' support the written-כתובה reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to show that the משנה's wording, 'she collects everything,' fits a case where the husband wrote her a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, since it teaches: 'she collects everything.' It works well if you say he wrote her a כתובה; that is why it teaches 'she collects everything.' But if you say he did not write her one,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings support from the wording of the משנה for the reading from step 10. The argument is not finished on this amud; it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says she collects 'everything.' That word makes sense if there is a written document, because she can collect everything written in it, including any extra the husband promised. The גמרא is setting up the other side: if nothing was written, what would 'everything' mean? That question is finished on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise (the wording also supports this)
It works well if you say

steps.confusionAlert: This step ends in the middle of a sentence. The words 'but if you say he did not write her one' are finished on the next amud, so do not look for the conclusion here.

phrases.english: The wording is also precise,
since it teaches: 'she collects everything.'
It works well if you say that he wrote her a כתובה;

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּקָא תָּנֵי גּוֹבֶה אֶת הַכֹּל.
phrases.english: that is why it teaches 'she collects everything.'
phrases.notes: 'Everything' means everything written in the document, even extra money the husband added beyond the basic amount.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ דְּלָא כְּתַב לַהּ,
phrases.english: But if you say that he did not write her one,

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי, דְּקָתָנֵי: גּוֹבָה אֶת הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the reading in steps 11 and 12, the גמרא brings support for it from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The reading from step 10 that the משנה is about a woman whose husband wrote her a כתובה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'גובה את הכל' (she collects everything), which fits best when there is a written document.
